familyTitle: Missing number when counting on in hundreds

c.v: Count on in hundreds to fill in the blank.
Counting on in hundreds means adding 100 each time.
Check: 5900 + 100 = 6000, which is the next number in the pattern.

familyTitle: Which row counts on in thousands

c.v: Which row shows counting on in thousands?
Counting on in thousands means adding 1000 each time. Only the thousands digit goes up, by 1 each time.
Row B is 4050, 5050, 6050, 7050. The thousands digit goes 4, 5, 6, 7.
Row A counts on in hundreds. Row C counts on in tens. Row D counts on in 500s.

familyTitle: How many numbers when counting on in hundreds

c.v: Raju counts on in hundreds. He starts at 3250 and stops at 4550. He says every number from 3250 to 4550.
How many numbers does he say in all, including 3250 and 4550?
1300 is 13 hundreds, so Raju counts on 13 times after saying 3250.
He also says 3250 itself, so he says 13 + 1 = 14 numbers.
13 is a common mistake. It forgets to count the first number, 3250.

familyTitle: Two children count in hundreds and thousands

c.v: Haziq counts on in hundreds. He starts at 2750, so 2750 is the 1st number he says.
Wen Xin counts on in thousands. She starts at 1750, so 1750 is the 1st number she says.
How much greater is Wen Xin's 3rd number than Haziq's 6th number?
Step 1: Haziq's 6th number is 5 counts on from 2750. 5 hundreds = 500, and 2750 + 500 = 3250.
Step 2: Wen Xin's 3rd number is 2 counts on from 1750. 2 thousands = 2000, and 1750 + 2000 = 3750.
Wen Xin's 3rd number is 500 greater than Haziq's 6th number.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds Haziq's 6th number: 3250
Finds Wen Xin's 3rd number: 3750

familyTitle: Find the first number when counting back

c.v: Aaron counts back in hundreds. The 5th number he says is 6350.
What is the 1st number he says?
Counting back means each number is 100 less than the one before it.
From the 1st number to the 5th number, Aaron counts back 4 times, so the 5th number is 4 hundreds less than the 1st number.
So the 1st number is 4 hundreds more than 6350: 6350 + 400 = 6750.

partialMarks.criterion: Sees that there are 4 counts (not 5) from the 1st number to the 5th number

familyTitle: Two children count towards each other

c.v: Aisha counts on in hundreds from 2300. Bryan counts back in hundreds from 3900.
They say their 1st numbers at the same time (Aisha says 2300 and Bryan says 3900). Then they say their 2nd numbers at the same time, and so on.
At one moment, they both say the same number at the same time. What is that number?
Step 1: Write out what each child says.
Step 2: Look at the 9th number each child says. Both say 3100 at the same time.
The number is 3100.

partialMarks.criterion: Writes out Aisha's numbers going up in hundreds and Bryan's numbers going down in hundreds
Finds that the 9th numbers match

familyTitle: Library books grow by a thousand each year

c.v: At the end of 2019, a library had 2480 books. Every year after that, the library got 1000 more books.
In which year did the library first have more than 5000 books?
Step 1: Count on in thousands from 2480, one year at a time.
Step 2: 4480 is not more than 5000, but 5480 is more than 5000.
The library first had more than 5000 books in 2022.

partialMarks.criterion: Counts on in thousands: 3480, 4480, 5480
Finds that 5480 is the first number more than 5000 and gives the year

familyTitle: Read a place-value chart

c.v: The place-value chart shows a number.
What is the number?
The chart shows 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones.
The 0 must stay in the hundreds place. 472 leaves it out, and that changes the value of the other digits.

familyTitle: Digit in the hundreds place

c.v: Which digit is in the hundreds place of 6580?
The places from the right are ones, tens, hundreds and thousands.
In 6580, the ones digit is 0, the tens digit is 8, the hundreds digit is 5 and the thousands digit is 6.
The digit in the hundreds place is 5.

familyTitle: Which number has a digit worth 600

c.v: In which number does the digit 6 have a value of 600?
A digit worth 600 must be in the hundreds place.
In 4638, the 6 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 600.
In 2961 the 6 is in the tens place (value 60). In 1326 the 6 is in the ones place (value 6). In 6314 the 6 is in the thousands place (value 6000).

familyTitle: Digit cards with place value clues

c.v: Jia Hao has four digit cards: 3, 0, 6 and 8. He uses all four cards to make a 4-digit number.
In his number, the digit 8 has a value of 8000 and the digit 6 has a value of 60.
What is the greatest number he can make?
Step 1: The digit 8 is worth 8000, so 8 is in the thousands place. The digit 6 is worth 60, so 6 is in the tens place.
Step 2: The cards 3 and 0 are left for the hundreds place and the ones place.
Step 3: For the greatest number, put the greater card (3) in the hundreds place and 0 in the ones place.
The number is 8360. The other choice is 8063, which is smaller.

partialMarks.criterion: Puts 8 in the thousands place and 6 in the tens place

familyTitle: Number riddle with place value clues

c.v: I am a 4-digit number.
The value of my hundreds digit is 300. My tens digit is 2 more than my hundreds digit. My ones digit is 0. My thousands digit is the sum of my hundreds digit and my tens digit.
What number am I?
Step 1: The value of the hundreds digit is 300, so the hundreds digit is 3.
Step 2: The tens digit is 2 more than 3, so the tens digit is 5. The ones digit is 0.
Step 3: The thousands digit is the sum of 3 and 5, so it is 8.
The number is 8350.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the hundreds digit 3 and the tens digit 5
Finds the thousands digit 8

familyTitle: Game scores from place value parts

c.v: Dylan's game score is made up of 3 thousands, 14 hundreds and 8 tens. Nurul's game score is 4350.
How many more points does Dylan score than Nurul?
Step 1: Find Dylan's score. 3 thousands = 3000, 14 hundreds = 1400 and 8 tens = 80.
Step 2: Dylan's score is greater than Nurul's score, so subtract: 4480 − 4350 = 130.
Dylan scores 130 more points than Nurul.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds Dylan's score: 4480
Subtracts 4350 from Dylan's score

familyTitle: Regroup hundreds and tens

c.v: Which number is the same as 9 hundreds and 14 tens?
914 and 9140 come from writing the 9 and the 14 side by side. 1400 is 14 hundreds, not 14 tens.

familyTitle: Change one digit and find the difference

c.v: Joel wrote the number 5724. He changed the digit 7 to a 3.
How much smaller is the new number than 5724?
The digit 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 700.
The new number is 5324, where the digit 3 is worth 300.
The number went down by 700 − 300 = 400. Check: 5724 − 5324 = 400.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds that the changed digit is in the hundreds place (700 changes to 300) or writes the new number 5324

familyTitle: 10 less across a zero

c.v: What number is 10 less than 6200?
6200 is 6 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones.
There are no tens to take away from, so regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens. Now there are 6 thousands, 1 hundred and 10 tens.
Take away 1 ten. That leaves 6 thousands, 1 hundred and 9 tens, which is 6190.

familyTitle: Words to numerals

c.v: Write this number in numerals.
Seven thousand, four hundred and twenty =
Seven thousand is 7000. Four hundred is 400. Twenty is 20.

familyTitle: Numerals to words

c.v: Write 4260 in words.

accepted: four thousand, two hundred and sixty
four thousand two hundred and sixty
four thousand, two hundred, and sixty
four thousand, two hundred and sixty.
four thousand two hundred and sixty.
four thousand, two hundred, and sixty.

c.v: 4260 has 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones.
4 thousands is "four thousand". 2 hundreds is "two hundred". 6 tens is "sixty".
The answer is "four thousand, two hundred and sixty".

familyTitle: Choose the words for a number with a zero

c.v: Which shows 8014 in words?
eight thousand, one hundred and four
eight thousand and forty
eight hundred and fourteen
eight thousand and fourteen
8014 has 8 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten and 4 ones. The last two digits, 14, are read as "fourteen".
So 8014 is "eight thousand and fourteen".
"Eight thousand, one hundred and four" is 8104. "Eight thousand and forty" is 8040. "Eight hundred and fourteen" is 814.

familyTitle: Read a number in words, then add 100

c.v: Hui Ling writes "two thousand, four hundred and six" in numerals. Then she adds 100 to her number.
What number does she get?
Step 1: "Two thousand, four hundred and six" is 2406.
Step 2: Adding 100 makes the hundreds digit 1 more, from 4 to 5. 2406 + 100 = 2506.
2416 adds 10 and 3406 adds 1000.

familyTitle: Numeral for a number with two zeros

c.v: Which numeral shows "nine thousand and nine"?
"Nine thousand" is 9000 and "nine" is 9 ones.
There are no hundreds and no tens, so write 0 in both places: 9009.
909 leaves out the thousands place. 9090 puts the 9 in the tens place. 9900 puts the second 9 in the hundreds place.

familyTitle: Words for the number after 9999

c.v: The greatest 4-digit number is 9999. What number comes right after it? Write the number in words.
The number after 9999 is 9999 + 1 = 10 000.
10 000 is 10 thousands and nothing else, so we write it as "ten thousand".

familyTitle: One less than a number given in words

c.v: What number is 1 less than "seven thousand and ten"? Write your answer in numerals.
Step 1: "Seven thousand and ten" is 7010.
Step 2: 1 less than 7010. There are 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones, which leaves 0 tens and 10 ones. Take away 1 one to get 9 ones.

partialMarks.criterion: Writes "seven thousand and ten" correctly as 7010

familyTitle: Prices written in words

c.v: Mr Lim's receipt shows the price of a television as "two thousand, four hundred and five dollars" and the price of a fridge as "one thousand and ninety dollars".
How much did Mr Lim pay for both items?
Step 1: Write both prices in numerals. The television is $2405. The fridge is $1090.
Step 2: Add the two prices: 2405 + 1090 = 3495.
Mr Lim paid $3495 for both items.

partialMarks.criterion: Writes both prices in numerals: $2405 and $1090
Adds the two prices correctly

familyTitle: Lucky draw number in words

c.v: In a lucky draw, the ticket number for first prize is "four thousand, seven hundred and two". The ticket number for second prize is 100 more than the ticket number for first prize.
Write the ticket number for second prize in words.

accepted: four thousand, eight hundred and two
four thousand eight hundred and two
four thousand, eight hundred, and two
four thousand, eight hundred and two.
four thousand eight hundred and two.
four thousand, eight hundred, and two.

c.v: Step 1: "Four thousand, seven hundred and two" is 4702.
Step 2: 100 more than 4702 is 4802. Only the hundreds digit changes, from 7 to 8.
Step 3: 4802 in words is "four thousand, eight hundred and two".

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the second prize number in numerals: 4802

familyTitle: Compare lucky numbers written in words

c.v: Gita, Hakim and Irfan each wrote their lucky number in words.
Gita: six thousand and ninety-nine
Hakim: six thousand, one hundred and nine
Irfan: six thousand, nine hundred and ten
What is the difference between the greatest number and the smallest number?
Step 1: Write each number in numerals. Gita's number is 6099. Hakim's number is 6109. Irfan's number is 6910.
Step 2: All three have 6 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 0 hundreds is the least and 9 hundreds is the most. Gita's 6099 is the smallest and Irfan's 6910 is the greatest.

partialMarks.criterion: Writes all three numbers in numerals: 6099, 6109 and 6910
Picks the greatest (6910) and the smallest (6099)

familyTitle: Pick the number smaller than a given number

c.v: Which number is smaller than 6048?
All the numbers have 6 thousands, so compare the hundreds.
6804 and 6408 have more hundreds than 6048, so they are greater.
6084 and 6048 both have 0 hundreds. Compare the tens: 8 tens is more than 4 tens, so 6084 is greater.
6040 has 4 tens, the same as 6048, and 0 ones is less than 8 ones. So 6040 is smaller than 6048.

familyTitle: Choose the comparison sign

c.v: Write >, < or = in the blank.
Both numbers have 4 thousands and 8 hundreds, so compare the tens.
4807 has 0 tens and 4870 has 7 tens. 0 tens is less than 7 tens.

familyTitle: Find the second smallest number

c.v: Look at these numbers.
Which number is the 2nd smallest?
All the numbers have 5 thousands. Compare the hundreds.
5012 has 0 hundreds, so it is the smallest. 5201 has 2 hundreds, so it is the greatest.
5102 and 5120 both have 1 hundred. Compare the tens: 0 tens is less than 2 tens, so 5102 is smaller than 5120.
From smallest to greatest: 5012, 5102, 5120, 5201. The 2nd smallest number is 5102.

familyTitle: Whole numbers between two numbers

c.v: How many whole numbers are there between 2998 and 3003? Do not count 2998 and 3003.
List the numbers after 2998 and before 3003: 2999, 3000, 3001, 3002.
There are 4 numbers.
Another way: 3003 − 2998 = 5, and one less than that is 4, because 3003 is not counted.

familyTitle: Cheapest and dearest phone

c.v: A shop sells four phones. The table shows the price of each phone.
Mr Ong buys the cheapest phone. Ms Lim buys the most expensive phone. How much more does Ms Lim pay than Mr Ong?
Step 1: All the prices have 4 thousands. Compare the hundreds.
$4083 has 0 hundreds, so it is the cheapest. $4803 has 8 hundreds, so it is the most expensive.
Step 2: Ms Lim pays $4803 and Mr Ong pays $4083. 4803 − 4083 = 720.
Ms Lim pays $720 more than Mr Ong.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the cheapest price ($4083)
Finds the most expensive price ($4803)

familyTitle: Smallest number above 3000 with different digits

c.v: What is the smallest 4-digit number greater than 3000 in which all four digits are different?
The number must be greater than 3000, so keep 3 in the thousands place and make the other digits as small as possible.
The hundreds digit can be 0. The tens digit cannot be 0 or 3 again, so the smallest is 1. The ones digit cannot be 0, 1 or 3, so the smallest is 2.
The number is 3012. Numbers such as 3001 and 3010 repeat a digit.

partialMarks.criterion: Keeps 3 in the thousands place and uses 0 in the hundreds place

familyTitle: Next number in an add-400 pattern

c.v: Look at this number pattern.
What is the next number?
Find how much the numbers go up each time: 2000 − 1600 = 400.
The next number is 2800 + 400 = 3200.

familyTitle: Missing number in a number pattern going down

c.v: Complete the number pattern.
The numbers go down by 200 each time: 5400 − 5200 = 200.

familyTitle: Which number is in the pattern

c.v: Look at this number pattern.
Which of these numbers is in the pattern?
The numbers go up by 300 each time.
Keep counting on in 300s: 3000, 3300, 3600, 3900.
3900 is in the pattern. 3400, 3500 and 3700 are skipped.

familyTitle: Work back to the first number

c.v: The numbers in a pattern go up by the same amount each time.
The 4th number is 4350 and the 5th number is 4650.
What is the 1st number?
Step 1: The numbers go up by 4650 − 4350 = 300 each time.
Step 2: To go back from the 4th number to the 1st number, take away 300 three times: 4350 − 900 = 3450.
3750 is the 2nd number and 4050 is the 3rd number.

familyTitle: Find the 5th number from a rule

c.v: The 1st number in a pattern is 150. The rule is: add 250 each time.
What is the 5th number in the pattern?
The 5th number is 4 steps on from the 1st number. 4 × 250 = 1000, and 150 + 1000 = 1150.

partialMarks.criterion: Adds 250 four times (not five times) or writes the list up to 900

familyTitle: Position of a number in a pattern

c.v: Look at this number pattern.
The number 2800 is in the pattern. Which number in the pattern is 2800? Write your answer as a number. For example, write 5 for the 5th number.
The numbers go up by 300 each time.
2800 is the 7th number. Another way: 2800 − 1000 = 1800 and 1800 is 6 steps of 300, so it is the 6 + 1 = 7th number.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds that the numbers go up by 300 each time

familyTitle: Museum visitors follow a pattern

c.v: A museum had 2150 visitors on Monday. Each day after that, the number of visitors went up by 250. This carried on until Friday.
How many visitors did the museum have on Thursday and Friday altogether?
Step 1: List the number of visitors each day. Monday 2150, Tuesday 2400, Wednesday 2650, Thursday 2900, Friday 3150.
Step 2: Add Thursday and Friday: 2900 + 3150 = 6050.
The museum had 6050 visitors on Thursday and Friday altogether.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds Thursday's visitors: 2900
Finds Friday's visitors: 3150

familyTitle: Pattern that goes up by two different amounts

c.v: Look at this number pattern.
The numbers go up by 500, then by 1000, then by 500, then by 1000, and so on.
What is the 10th number in the pattern?
Step 1: Write the pattern out: 1st 2000, 2nd 2500, 3rd 3500, 4th 4000, 5th 5000, 6th 5500.
The 10th number is 8500.

partialMarks.criterion: Sees that the pattern goes up by 500 and 1000 in turn
Carries on the pattern to the 9th number (8000)

familyTitle: Missing first number in a pattern

c.v: Complete the number pattern.
The numbers go up by 200 each time: 2850 − 2650 = 200.
The first number is 200 less than 2650: 2650 − 200 = 2450.
